userStories.title: Fix Wizard Navigation Bug (P0)
userStories.description: [Bug][Frontend] OptimizationWizard closes unexpectedly after completing Step 2 (Strategy selection). Root cause: 958-line component with complex useEffect dependencies causing state resets. This is the #1 priority from cross-agent consensus matrix - all 4 agents rated PRIORITY.
acceptanceCriteria: PHASE 0 - PREP: Read frontend/maestro-ui/src/components/OptimizationWizard.js fully (~958 lines)
PHASE 0 - PREP: Map all useState hooks and their initial values
PHASE 0 - PREP: Map all useEffect hooks and their dependency arrays - especially lines 156-174 with initialPreset
PHASE 0 - PREP: Identify which useEffect causes activeStep to reset when it shouldn't
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Add console.log to track activeStep changes and identify trigger
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Fix the root cause - either guard the useEffect or refactor to useReducer
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: If using useReducer, create wizardReducer with actions: SET_STEP, UPDATE_FORM_DATA, RESET_WIZARD
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Ensure initialPreset changes do NOT reset activeStep to 0
PHASE 2 - TEST: Run npm run build in frontend/maestro-ui - must succeed with no errors
PHASE 2 - TEST: Start frontend with npm start, navigate to localhost:3000
PHASE 2 - TEST: Click '+ New Optimization' button, verify wizard opens at Step 1
PHASE 2 - TEST: Fill Step 1 fields (provider, symbol, timeframe), click Next - verify Step 2 loads
PHASE 2 - TEST: Fill Step 2 fields (strategy), click Next - verify Step 3 loads (NOT closing)
PHASE 2 - TEST: Click Back, verify Step 2 still has selected strategy
VALIDATE: Complete all 4 steps, click Run - verify optimization starts and toast notification shows

context.debugTip: Add useEffect(() => console.log('activeStep changed:', activeStep), [activeStep]) to track resets
context.technicalDebt: Component is 958 lines - largest in codebase. Consider splitting after fix.
context.consensusRating: All 4 agents (Frontend Dev, Quant, Tech Lead, UX) rated PRIORITY

userStories.title: Create useAsyncData Hook for Consistent Loading (P1)
userStories.description: [Feature][Frontend] Standardize loading states across 50+ instances of loading/isLoading patterns with no shared abstraction. Create reusable hook that provides consistent loading, error, and data state management.
acceptanceCriteria: PHASE 0 - PREP: Run grep -r 'loading' frontend/maestro-ui/src/components/ to find all loading patterns
PHASE 0 - PREP: Note inconsistent patterns in: DataManagement.js, Home.js, OptimizationForm.js, CandleStickChart.js
PHASE 0 - PREP: Check if @tanstack/react-query is in package.json (it's installed but unused)
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Create frontend/maestro-ui/src/hooks/useAsyncData.js
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Export function useAsyncData(fetchFn, deps = []) that returns { data, loading, error, refetch }
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Use useState for data/loading/error, useEffect to call fetchFn, useCallback for refetch
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Set loading=true before fetch, loading=false in .then()/.catch()
PHASE 2 - TEST: Update Home.js to use useAsyncData for fetching providers list
PHASE 2 - TEST: Add <Skeleton variant='rectangular' height={200} /> when loading
PHASE 2 - TEST: Run npm run build - must succeed
PHASE 2 - TEST: Refresh Home page, verify skeleton shows briefly then content loads
VALIDATE: No layout shift when data loads - skeleton and content have same dimensions

context.hookTemplate: export function useAsyncData(fetchFn, deps = []) { const [state, setState] = useState({ data: null, loading: true, error: null }); useEffect(() => { fetchFn().then(data => setState({ data, loading: false, error: null })).catch(error => setState({ data: null, loading: false, error })); }, deps); return { ...state, refetch: () => fetchFn() }; }
context.alternativeApproach: Could also use @tanstack/react-query useQuery for caching benefits
context.consensusRating: 3 of 4 agents (Frontend Dev, Tech Lead, UX) rated PRIORITY

userStories.title: Add CSV Export Backend Endpoint (P2)
userStories.description: [Feature][Backend] Add REST endpoint to export optimization results as CSV for external analysis in Python/R/Excel. Quants rated this 10/10 - critical for professional workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: PHASE 0 - PREP: Read backend/main/rest_api.py to understand Flask endpoint patterns
PHASE 0 - PREP: Find existing /optimization/results/<tid> endpoint as reference
PHASE 0 - PREP: Check RethinkDB optimization_results table schema for available fields
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Import csv and io modules at top of rest_api.py
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Add route @app.route('/optimization/results/<tid>/export/csv', methods=['GET'])
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Query optimization_results table: r.db('filos-dev').table('optimization_results').get(tid)
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Extract key metrics: test_name, strategy, symbol, bin_size, sharpe_ratio, total_pnl, win_rate, max_drawdown
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Write to StringIO with csv.writer, return Response(output.getvalue(), mimetype='text/csv')
PHASE 1 - IMPLEMENT: Add Content-Disposition header: response.headers['Content-Disposition'] = f'attachment; filename={test_name}.csv'
PHASE 2 - TEST: Start backend with python rest_api.py
PHASE 2 - TEST: Get a valid tid from /optimization/results endpoint
PHASE 2 - TEST: curl -s http://localhost:5050/optimization/results/{tid}/export/csv - verify CSV output
VALIDATE: CSV has header row and data row with correct values matching the optimization result

context.downloadPattern: const handleExport = async () => { const response = await fetch(`${API_URL}/optimization/results/${tid}/export/csv`); const blob = await response.blob(); const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob); const a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = url; a.download = `${testName}_export.csv`; document.body.appendChild(a); a.click(); document.body.removeChild(a); URL.revokeObjectURL(url); };
